title: Epic: Hardware tuning profiles pack (H100/B200/L40S) for serving runtime
creator: Talia Benson
dependencies: Perf canary capacity on L40S runners (see INT-8832)
B200 limited fleet access + driver/CUDA stack availability (Infra)
description:
Goal
Deliver a versioned, safe-by-default “hardware tuning profiles pack” for Redwood’s serving runtime with curated kernel + scheduler + memory/KV-cache presets per GPU SKU (H100, B200, L40S). Profiles must be measurable, easy to roll out across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and have clear guardrails + rollback semantics.

Why this matters
- Strengthens “Redwood-verified performance profiles” story in the model catalog
- Reduces incident volume from ad-hoc/mis-tuned runtime settings
- Establishes a repeatable bring-up process for new GPU generations (B200 now; future SKUs later)

In scope
- Profile schema + loader + validation; versioning and compatibility rules
- Hardware detection + normalization for fleet variance (PCIe vs SXM, provider SKU strings, MIG, multi-GPU nodes)
- Kernel auto-selection heuristics per SKU (sequence length buckets where relevant)
- Scheduler presets (continuous batching, prefill/decode fairness, backpressure/queue limits)
- KV cache memory behavior presets + budgeting (esp. L40S)
- Perf/benchmark harness updates + reproducibility
- Perf-canary regression gates + dashboards + alert routing
- Documentation: expected behavior (latency/throughput curves, workload envelope, known trade-offs)
- Staged rollout plan + rollback plan (per pool/region; override order and “kill switches”)

Out of scope (initial)
- Writing new kernels from scratch
- Major API surface changes for customers
- Customer-specific bespoke tuning (handled via Solutions/Support follow-ups)

Success metrics (acceptance criteria)
We will treat these as “expected behavior” (not contractual guarantees) and gate via perf-canary + staged rollout:
- No new P0/P1 incidents attributable to profile changes during rollout window
- H100: throughput improvement on representative workloads with bounded tail latency
  - Target: +8–15% tokens/sec at equal p95 (or ≤ +5% p95 regression with ≥ +15% tokens/sec, only in throughput-first mode)
- L40S: materially reduced OOM/retry rate under long-context workloads
  - Target: ≥ 80% reduction in OOM-related failures in workload-matrix “long context + moderate concurrency” runs; stable p95 within agreed envelope
- B200: enablement with explicit experimental gating
  - Target: functional parity baseline + stable canary with rollback playbook proven; perf deltas tracked but not required for GA
- Observability: ability to answer “what profile is active, why, and what changed?” within 5 minutes of oncall investigation
  - Target: profile selection + override source available in metrics + runtime logs + debug endpoint/CLI

Milestones / plan (8–10 weeks, rolling)
1) Kickoff + requirements (Week 1)
- Confirm target SKUs (H100/L40S first, B200 gated)
- Define safety constraints and workload envelope assumptions

2) Baselines (Weeks 1–2)
- Lock workload matrix + harness; collect baseline curves per GPU SKU

3) Schema + implementation (Weeks 2–5)
- Finalize profile schema, inheritance, and compatibility checks
- Implement runtime loader + override precedence

4) Validation + canary (Weeks 5–8)
- Perf-canary thresholds + noise reduction
- Staged rollout by pool/region; regressions triaged with quick disable path

5) Docs + release (Weeks 7–10)
- Expected behavior docs + runbooks + release notes
- Internal training for oncall/SRE/Support

Definition of done
- Profile pack v1.0 (H100, L40S) enabled by default in at least one hosted region/pool with successful staged rollout
- B200 profile present but behind experimental gating with explicit compatibility/stack checks
- Perf suite emits standardized artifacts (curves + summary) per SKU and per profile version
- Perf-canary gates live pre-merge and post-deploy, with documented thresholds and alert routing
- Runbook + known-issues doc + rollback criteria published
- Support-ready: docs for Private overrides (Helm) and a CLI/debug endpoint to dump effective config

Risk register (tracked here; detailed in runbook/known-issues as needed)
1) Hardware variance breaks assumptions (HBM size, clocks, MIG/partitioning, PCIe vs SXM)
- Risk: profile tuned for one variant causes OOM or latency regression on another
- Mitigation: strict guardrails + detection normalization; compatibility matrix logged at startup; safe fallback to “baseline” profile when detection ambiguous

2) Throughput gains harm tail latency (scheduler fairness/backpressure)
- Risk: p95/p99 regressions lead to customer-visible latency spikes
- Mitigation: separate balanced vs throughput-first modes; perf-canary gates tied to p95; rollback criteria + quick disable per pool; regression tests added for fairness

3) B200 bring-up incomplete / unstable due to limited fleet access
- Risk: canary regressions or unknown kernel behaviors
- Mitigation: experimental flag, explicit driver/CUDA checks, staged regional rollout, documented fallback plan; do not GA B200 profile until stability signals are strong

4) Config drift between profile pack and runtime defaults
- Risk: operators can’t reason about changes; Private deployments diverge
- Mitigation: normalize default handling; loader prints “effective config”; integration tests for precedence; release notes include “what changed and why”

5) Perf-canary noise / false positives slow iteration
- Risk: blocked merges or alert fatigue
- Mitigation: tune thresholds; isolate noisy workloads; infra fixes for runner stability; document expected variance bands

6) Override complexity causes operational mistakes
- Risk: per-customer/per-pool overrides unexpectedly override safety settings
- Mitigation: ADR-defined precedence + “unsafe override” warnings; SRE-approved kill switch; guardrails disallow exceeding memory budgets by default

Open questions
- MIG handling: do we apply profile per physical GPU or per MIG instance? Current approach: treat MIG as a separate “device class” with conservative defaults; refine once we see real usage.
- Multi-GPU nodes: when model sharding is enabled, do we ever need per-node NCCL/collectives tuning in v1? (Currently: document as “where applicable” but keep default conservative; revisit post v1.)
- Contract language: docs must stay in “expected behavior” territory; verify with Docs/Legal phrasing guidance.

Rollout plan summary
- H100/L40S: staged by region/pool with 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% enablement, with minimum dwell time and perf-canary/alert gates at each step
- B200: experimental only; single pool canary; explicit opt-in with rapid rollback; do not expand without sponsor sign-off

Rollback criteria (initial; final values in runbook)
- Any sustained p95 regression above threshold for ≥ 30 minutes vs control, or OOM/retry rate above threshold, attributable to profile-enabled builds
- Customer escalations tied to profile rollout (Support/SRE triage) where disable returns metrics to baseline
